letters.excerpt: I often feel so infinitely indebted to you, and yet I try to express it so poorly. But I want you to know that my paintings exist because of your support. Without you, I would have sunk long ago.
letters.context: Written during the height of Van Gogh's Arles period, when he was painting Sunflowers and The Night Café.

letters.excerpt: I am unable to describe exactly what is the matter with me; now and then there are horrible fits of anxiety, apparently without cause, or otherwise a feeling of emptiness and fatigue in the head... and at times I have attacks of melancholy and of atrocious remorse.
letters.context: A rare candid admission of his mental health struggles, written months before the ear incident.

letters.excerpt: I dream of painting and then I paint my dream. The canvas has become a mirror of my inner life — every stroke a word I cannot speak with my mouth.
letters.context: Written while painting The Starry Night, reflecting his belief that art should express inner vision.

letters.excerpt: The sunflower is mine, in a way. It is a symbol of gratitude. I have wanted to do a painting that will be like a symphony of blue and yellow.
letters.context: Referring to his famous Sunflower series, painted to decorate Gauguin's room.

letters.excerpt: I feel a tremendous need for, shall I say the word — for religion — so I go outside at night to paint the stars. I always think that the night is more alive and more richly colored than the day.
letters.context: Written before painting The Starry Night, revealing his deep spiritual connection to the night sky.

letters.excerpt: What would life be if we had no courage to attempt anything? I am trying to do the impossible — to paint what I love so deeply that it becomes a prayer.
letters.context: Early in his artistic career, showing the determination that would define his life.

letters.excerpt: I want to touch people with my art. I want them to say, 'he feels deeply, he feels tenderly.' Art is to console those who are broken by life.
letters.context: Written after deciding to become an artist, articulating his philosophy of art's purpose.

letters.excerpt: The cypresses are always occupying my thoughts. I should like to make something of them like the canvases of the sunflowers. It is as beautiful of proportion as an Egyptian obelisk.
letters.context: Written while painting The Cypresses, one of his most iconic subjects.

letters.excerpt: I am in a state of terrible anxiety and yet I work with a certain ardour. I must paint on, paint on. It is the only thing that keeps me from going under completely.
letters.context: Written during a period of intense productivity and growing mental instability.

letters.excerpt: There is no blue without yellow and without orange. Colors, like music, vibrate with their own inner life. I try to understand the real significance of what we call abstraction.
letters.context: Revealing his theory of color harmony that would influence generations of artists.

letters.excerpt: I cannot help it that my paintings do not sell. The time will come when people will see that they are worth more than the price of the paint.
letters.context: A prophetic statement — he sold only one painting during his lifetime.

letters.excerpt: The thing is that we painters are always in the open air, in the fields. My God, how beautiful the countryside is. I am ravished by the thought of what I shall paint there.
letters.context: Written shortly after arriving in Arles, overwhelmed by the Provençal landscape.

letters.excerpt: I have a terrible need of — I might say the word — religion. Then I go out and paint the stars at night. It seems to me that the night is more alive than the day.
letters.context: Expressing the spiritual dimension that permeates all his work.

letters.excerpt: The olive trees with the white cloud and the rising moon study — I am not exaggerating when I say that it was so beautiful. Nature is so beautiful that it makes one weep.
letters.context: Written while painting his Olive Trees series, capturing the Provençal landscape.

letters.excerpt: I am doing what I cannot help doing. I am not an adventurer by choice but by fate, and feeling nowhere so much a stranger as in my own family.
letters.context: Early letter revealing the isolation and alienation that would mark his life.

letters.excerpt: The wheat fields are like the sea, infinite and beautiful. I am working on a new canvas — a field of wheat under a troubled sky.
letters.context: One of his last letters, referring to Wheatfield with Crows, painted days before his death.

letters.excerpt: I am trying to exaggerate the essential and to leave the obvious vague. Characteristic of the painter is to paint the essential.
letters.context: Articulating his artistic philosophy — expression over realism.

letters.excerpt: The more I think about it, the more I realize there is nothing more truly artistic than to love people. What I most want to do is to leave a certain souvenir in the form of drawings or pictures.
letters.context: Written at the very beginning of his artistic journey, defining his life's mission.

letters.excerpt: I have painted a landscape which I think you will like — a field of wheat after the rain. The effect of the wet earth and the golden grain is something I cannot describe.
letters.context: Describing his fascination with wheat fields that would become a recurring subject.

letters.excerpt: I feel that my work is a part of my faith. I cannot separate my art from my belief that there is something greater than ourselves in the beauty of nature.
letters.context: Revealing the spiritual foundation of his artistic practice.

letters.excerpt: The painter of the future is a colorist such as there has not yet been. I am trying to render intense color and not a grey harmony.
letters.context: Predicting the future of painting — he was that colorist.

letters.excerpt: I have a new canvas — a night effect, a café terrace lit by a large gas lamp. The night is more alive than the day, and the color is magnificent.
letters.context: Describing The Night Café, one of his most psychologically intense works.

letters.excerpt: The reaper in the sun — death is not sad, it happens in bright sunlight with all the glory of nature. I see the image of death in that setting sun.
letters.context: Reflecting on his painting The Reaper, revealing his complex relationship with mortality.

letters.excerpt: I am working like a madman. I have painted four still lifes — purple irises, a lilac bush, and two studies of roses. The garden is so beautiful.
letters.context: Written during a period of remarkable productivity at the asylum.

letters.excerpt: The portrait is the most intimate thing in painting. I want to paint men and women with that something of the eternal which the halo used to symbolize.
letters.context: Articulating his approach to portraiture — seeking the eternal in the human face.

letters.excerpt: I have just returned from the moors. It is magnificent — the deep black earth against the sky. I have never seen nature so beautiful.
letters.context: Written during his solitary journey to the Dutch moors, seeking raw nature.

letters.excerpt: The almond trees are beginning to blossom. I am working on a large canvas — white almond blossoms against a blue sky. It is my most delicate work.
letters.context: Referring to Almond Blossom, painted to celebrate the birth of his nephew.

letters.excerpt: I have a new study of a starry sky. It is a continuation of the night effects I have been doing. The stars are like flowers in a garden of night.
letters.context: Written while painting The Starry Night, his most celebrated work.

letters.excerpt: The doctor says I am much better. I have been painting in the garden — the irises are in bloom. Nature is my greatest medicine.
letters.context: Written shortly after voluntarily entering the asylum at Saint-Rémy.

letters.excerpt: I have done a portrait of Dr. Gachet. He is a strange man, suffering from the same melancholy as I. We understand each other in our sadness.
letters.context: One of his last letters, referring to Portrait of Dr. Gachet, which sold for $82 million in 1990.
